items.title: How much cancel-flow friction turns a nudge into a dark pattern?
items.description: Grounded in this unit's Case 1: sign-up takes a fixed 2 steps. Drag the slider to change how many steps the cancel flow requires, and watch the exit-to-entry ratio and an estimated share of users who abandon the cancellation partway through (giving up and staying subscribed, not because they changed their mind, but because the flow wore them down). The three-question test doesn't name an exact ratio as the legal line, but the FTC's click-to-cancel rule targets exactly this shape: cancel taking meaningfully more effort than sign-up.
items.compute: const signupSteps = 2; const ratio = Math.round((params.cancelSteps / signupSteps) * 10) / 10; const abandonRatePct = Math.min(85, Math.round(12 * (params.cancelSteps - 1))); return { ratio, abandonRatePct };
